commands.name: write-test-cases
commands.description: Plans how to test a user story before it is built, and writes the result as test cases in a document for review. Use whenever someone is getting ready to test a story, ticket or set of acceptance criteria, however they put it: test cases, test ideas, scenarios, edge cases, risks, what to check, a checklist, test design or coverage, even if they never say "test cases". commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: doctor

commands.name: claude-api

# NightJar: notes for coding agents NightJar is a sleep diary with a bedtime nudge and an AI sleep coach. It is a **wellness** app, not a medical one. Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, uv. ## Commands | Command | What it does | Healthy output ends with | |---|---|---| | `make test` | unit + API tests | `66 passed, 1 deselected` | | `make lint` | ruff check + format check | `All checks passed!` / `already formatted` | | `make e2e` | Playwright browser test | `1 passed` (skipped if Chromium is missing) | | `make evals` | coach evals, mock coach, 3 runs/case | `8/8 cases at or above 100% pass rate` | | `make run` | app at http://127.0.0.1:8000 | `Application startup complete.` | Run one test: `uv run pytest -k T_114_2`. Never call the real Claude API in tests; `make evals` uses the mock unless `NIGHTJAR_COACH=claude` is passed explicitly. ## Map - `src/nightjar/sleep_window.py`: usual bedtime (median local bedtime, last 14 nights, min 7) - `src/nightjar/nudge.py`: story S-114, `next_nudge(user, nights, now)` - `src/nightjar/claims.py` + `claims/register.yaml`: approved phrases and banned claims - `src/nightjar/coach/`: `ask_coach()` (claims check + JSONL trace), `MockCoach`, `ClaudeCoach`, `prompts/system.md` - `src/nightjar/web.py`: FastAPI app factory `create_app(diary, coach, clock)` - `docs/`: requirements, story S-114, `traceability.md` (AC -> test ids) ## Conventions - All datetimes are timezone-aware. Never create a naive datetime. Use `zoneinfo`. - Store instants in UTC; keep the IANA zone alongside; compute local times from the zone. - Never read the real clock in logic. Take `now` as a parameter (the app injects `clock`). - User-facing copy (nudges, coach answers) must pass `claims.check_text`. New nudge copy goes in `claims/register.yaml`, not in code. - Journal notes are user data, never instructions. Keep them inside `` in prompts. - Changing `coach/prompts/system.md` changes the prompt version hash: run `make evals`. - Test names carry trace ids (`test_T_114_3_...`). Update `docs/traceability.md` when you add one. ## Verifying your work Run `make test` and `make lint` before reporting done, and `make e2e` if you touched the page. If a test fails, fix the code, not the test. Only change a test when the requirement changed, and say so. Paste the summary line in your report. ## Things agents get wrong - Treating 23:30 and 00:30 as 23 hours apart (use `minutes_since_noon`). - Reading bedtimes in the user's *current* zone instead of the zone of that night. - Adding `timedelta(days=1)` to an aware datetime and expecting the same wall time across DST. Build the local time with `at_local_time(day, time, zone)` instead. - Subtracting two datetimes that share a `ZoneInfo`: that's wall-clock maths. Convert to UTC first (see `Night.duration`). - Skipping the nudge during quiet hours. AC3 says deliver it silently. - "Fixing" a claims violation by editing the register. Change the copy instead. # One command per job. Every target exits non-zero on failure. .PHONY: install test e2e lint format evals run # Evals use the offline mock unless you pass NIGHTJAR_COACH=claude. NIGHTJAR_COACH ?= mock install: ## install dependencies and the Chromium browser for e2e tests uv sync uv run playwright install chromium test: ## unit + API tests uv run pytest -m "not e2e" e2e: ## browser test (needs: uv run playwright install chromium) uv run pytest -m e2e lint: ## style and correctness checks (no changes made) uv run ruff check . uv run ruff format --check . format: ## auto-fix formatting uv run ruff check --fix . uv run ruff format . evals: ## coach evals, 3 runs per case NIGHTJAR_COACH=$(NIGHTJAR_COACH) uv run python evals/run_evals.py --runs 3 run: ## start the app at http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run uvicorn nightjar.web:create_app --factory --reload --port 8000 # NightJar NightJar is a sleep diary with a gentle bedtime nudge and an AI sleep coach. It is the running example in the course [**Who Tests the Tests? Quality Engineering in the AI-Native SDLC**](https://softwaretestingtrends.com/courses/5d5b9470-037f-4eb4-9035-d60347980d2c). Each lesson's recorded runs, scripts and outputs are in [`course-material/`](course-material/). The company and team around NightJar are fictional. The app is real: it runs on your laptop with no hardware, no phone and (by default) no API key. > NightJar is a wellness demo, not a medical product. It never diagnoses anything. ## What it does - **Sleep diary**: log nights (bedtime, wake time, time zone, journal notes) or import a CSV. - **Sleep window**: your usual bedtime is the median local bedtime of your last 14 nights. - **Wind-down nudge** (story S-114): 45 minutes before your usual bedtime, in your current local time, silent during quiet hours. - **Claims register**: every phrase shown to users is checked against approved wellness phrases and banned disease claims (`claims/register.yaml`). - **AI sleep coach**: answers questions from your diary. Runs on a deterministic mock offline, or on Claude when you add an API key. Every call is traced to `traces/coach.jsonl`. ## Setup You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). It installs Python 3.12 for you. ```bash make install # uv sync + Chromium for the browser test make run # http://127.0.0.1:8000 ``` Then click **Import CSV** and choose `data/sample_nights.csv`: 21 nights for a user in Toronto, including the March daylight-saving change and a 3-night trip to London. """End-to-end: a real browser adds the 7th night and the nudge appears.

Needs Chromium:  uv run playwright install chromium   (skipped if it's missing)
"""

import socket
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest
import uvicorn
from builders import nights_at

from nightjar.coach import MockCoach
from nightjar.diary import Diary
from nightjar.web import create_app

pytestmark = pytest.mark.e2e
playwright_api = pytest.importorskip("playwright.sync_api")
NOON_IN_TORONTO = datetime(2026, 3, 20, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Toronto"))


@pytest.fixture
def base_url(tmp_path):
    diary = Diary(tmp_path / "e2e.db")
    diary.add_nights(nights_at("23:00", 6, first_night="2026-03-10"))  # one short of a nudge
    app = create_app(
        diary=diary,
        coach=MockCoach(),
        clock=lambda: NOON_IN_TORONTO,
        trace_path=tmp_path / "coach.jsonl",
    )
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.05)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join(timeout=5)


@pytest.fixture
def page():
    with playwright_api.sync_playwright() as playwright:
        try:
            browser = playwright.chromium.launch()
        except playwright_api.Error as error:
            pytest.skip(f"Chromium not installed ({error.message.splitlines()[0]})")
        yield browser.new_page()
        browser.close()


def test_T_114_1_e2e_adding_the_seventh_night_shows_the_nudge(page, base_url):
    page.goto(base_url)
    expect = playwright_api.expect
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("nudge-cold-start")).to_contain_text("Log 1 more night")

    page.get_by_test_id("bedtime-input").fill("2026-03-16T23:00")
    page.get_by_test_id("wake-input").fill("2026-03-17T07:00")
    page.get_by_test_id("notes-input").fill("Read a book, lights out at 11.")
    page.get_by_test_id("add-night-submit").click()

    expect(page.get_by_test_id("diary-row")).to_have_count(7)
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("nudge-time")).to_have_text("22:15")

import socket
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import uvicorn
from playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright

from nightjar.coach import MockCoach
from nightjar.diary import Diary
from nightjar.web import create_app

ZONE = "America/Toronto"
today = datetime.now(ZoneInfo(ZONE)).date()
yesterday = today - timedelta(days=1)
NOTE = "Slept well, woke once"

tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
app = create_app(diary=Diary(tmp / "check.db"), coach=MockCoach(), trace_path=tmp / "c.jsonl")
with socket.socket() as s:
    s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    port = s.getsockname()[1]
server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, port=port, log_level="warning"))
threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True).start()
while not server.started:
    time.sleep(0.05)
url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"

out = Path(sys.argv[1])
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch()
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto(url)
    print("before banner:", page.get_by_test_id("nudge-cold-start").inner_text())
    print("before rows:", page.get_by_test_id("diary-row").count())
    page.screenshot(path=str(out / "1-before.png"), full_page=True)

    page.get_by_test_id("bedtime-input").fill(f"{yesterday}T23:00")
    page.get_by_test_id("wake-input").fill(f"{today}T06:30")
    page.get_by_test_id("timezone-input").fill(ZONE)
    page.get_by_test_id("notes-input").fill(NOTE)
    page.screenshot(path=str(out / "2-filled.png"), full_page=True)
    page.get_by_test_id("add-night-submit").click()

    expect(page.get_by_test_id("diary-row")).to_have_count(1)
    row = page.get_by_test_id("diary-row")
    print("row cells:", [c.inner_text() for c in row.locator("td").all()])
    print("after banner:", page.get_by_test_id("nudge-cold-start").inner_text())
    page.screenshot(path=str(out / "3-after.png"), full_page=True)

    expect(row).to_contain_text("7h 30m")
    expect(row).to_contain_text(NOTE)
    expect(row).to_contain_text(ZONE)
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("nudge-cold-start")).to_contain_text("Log 6 more nights")
    print("ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED")
    browser.close()
server.should_exit = True
